title: NFL Owners Unanimously Approve $9.612 Billion Sale of Seahawks to Khosla Family
dek: NFL team owners voted unanimously to ratify the $9.612 billion sale of the Seattle Seahawks to a group led by venture capitalist Vinod Khosla's family, marking the largest franchise transaction in NFL history. The sale ends nearly three decades of ownership by the Paul Allen family and transfers a reigning Super Bowl champion to new leadership.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The $9.612 billion Seahawks sale represents a 59 percent increase over the previous NFL record, the $6.05 billion Commanders purchase in 2023.
bottom_line: The sale closes next month, clearing the way for Neeru Khosla to assume controlling ownership. Watch whether the Khosla family announces the remaining investors in their ownership group and whether existing front office staff remain in place, and whether the franchise's technology-sector leadership produces operational changes in its first season under new ownership.
body: NFL team owners voted unanimously Wednesday to ratify the $9.612 billion sale of the Seattle Seahawks to a group led by venture capitalist Vinod Khosla's family, ending nearly three decades of ownership by the Paul Allen estate. The transaction is the largest franchise purchase in NFL history.

The vote took place during a special one-day league meeting at an Atlanta airport hotel. Per Front Office Sports, the owners on the NFL's finance and ownership policy committees had voted unanimously the prior week to recommend approval of the purchase.

Neeru Khosla, Vinod Khosla's wife, will serve as the franchise's controlling owner, with their son Neal Khosla to have a role in ownership. Vinod Khosla, 71, is the co-founder of Sun Microsystems and founder of Khosla Ventures. According to Front Office Sports, Forbes estimates his net worth at 13.4 billion dollars.

Vinod Khosla stated at the meeting: "As Roger (Goodell) said, it's pretty simple when the team is functioning as well as it is today. How often do you get to buy a franchise that just won the Super Bowl? So we are incredibly lucky and humbled by this gift from the Allen trust." He added: "The task ahead is actually pretty simple: Keep the winning streak alive. Get another Super Bowl. That's simple. In general, our approach is generally going to be long-term focused. That's our inclination always."

The Seahawks beat the Patriots in February in Santa Clara for their second Super Bowl title under the Allen family's ownership. Per Front Office Sports, the team has a devoted fan base, a respected front office led by executive John Schneider, and coach Mike Macdonald.

The sale price represents a 59 percent increase over the previous NFL record. Per Front Office Sports, private equity investor Josh Harris led a group that purchased the Washington Commanders from Daniel Snyder for 6.05 billion dollars in 2023. The Khosla family holds a minority ownership stake in the 49ers and must divest itself of that interest. Front Office Sports notes that similar divestiture situations "sometimes have taken months to resolve," but the sources do not specify a timeline.

Paul Allen purchased an option to buy the Seahawks in 1996 and completed the 194 million dollar deal in 1997. He died in 2018 and directed that the Seahawks and his NBA team, the Trail Blazers, be sold and the proceeds donated to charity. Jody Allen, his sister, served as the Seahawks' de facto owner as trustee of her brother's trust. The estate commenced the sale process following the Super Bowl, with investment bank Allen & Company and law firm Latham & Watkins overseeing the transaction.
The deal is expected to close next month. The Seahawks are scheduled to host the NFL's season-opening game September 9 against the Patriots at Lumen Field in Seattle.
